CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on assessing the impact of recent treatment modifications.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his scheduled follow-up appointment, reporting a stable overall condition with slight improvements noted in his sleep patterns and headache frequency since his last visit. He indicates that he has been averaging 7-8 hours of sleep per night, with only occasional nocturnal awakenings, which he finds manageable. However, he still experiences some difficulty with sleep initiation, particularly on nights when he feels more anxious.
The patient reports that his tension-type headaches have further decreased to approximately once a week, with an intensity of 1-2 out of 10. He continues to use ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, stating that the medication remains effective without any adverse effects. Mr. Smith attributes this continued improvement to his commitment to physical activity, mindfulness exercises, and ongoing cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), which he finds increasingly beneficial.
Mr. Smith has been diligent in attending his bi-weekly acupuncture sessions, which he believes have contributed positively to his stress management and relaxation. He also notes that he has been practicing progressive muscle relaxation techniques, which have helped him manage anxiety symptoms more effectively.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (stable usage) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to thrive in his role as a software engineer, implementing effective strategies for managing work-related stress. He remains active in his running group, which he finds instrumental for both physical fitness and mental clarity. His dietary habits continue to reflect a balanced diet, with consistent abstinence from alcohol and limited caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Notable improvements in sleep quality; anxiety remains well-controlled; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Further reduced headache frequency; intensity mild; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue has shown slight improvement; no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/72 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-rested and engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with reduced anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Lorazepam remains at 1 mg as needed. Continue to reinforce the importance of regular CBT attendance and mindfulness exercises to further enhance anxiety management. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg. Monitor sleep quality closely for any signs of regression. Consider the addition of sleep hygiene education to optimize sleep environment. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Maintain amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Given the further reduction in headache frequency, consider follow-up in three months to reassess and potentially taper medications if symptoms remain stable. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to persist with physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue does not further improve, consider referral to a sleep specialist for comprehensive evaluation.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-11-01 to continue monitoring symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
